patch_description:
The original program failed validation because it returned an empty list `[]` for `column_orderings` (no valid per-row column permutations) and its recursive logic was broken (row/column recursion reassembled data via `pd.DataFrame(values.tolist())` losing dtypes and row identity, thread-pool futures consumed with `as_completed` wrote rows to arbitrary positions, an "original_index" column was fabricated, and the final `sort_values` scrambled rows). The output rows therefore did not correspond to the input rows and no consistent per-row orderings were supplied.

The fix replaces the broken recursion with a clean, bounded construction-selection algorithm: (1) keep the data frame untouched (values, rows, shape preserved, object dtype), (2) build up to three candidate per-row column orderings — original order, a global frequency-ranked order scored by sum(len(v)*count*(count-1)), and a conditional partition tree that picks, within each row group, the column with the largest length-weighted repetition and puts it first for those rows — (3) score each candidate with the true serial character-Trie objective (sum of adjacent LCPs of the sorted serialized row strings, computed with C-speed slice comparisons), and (4) return the best candidate's per-row orderings along with the unchanged data. Missing values serialize to "" only for scoring; stored cells are never modified. col_merge/one_way_dep parameters are accepted and handled with the existing API helpers without altering stored values.
